spec_features.spec_quote: open-ended "run until meltdown" loops; any objective that rewards producing more distressed output
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:88 `for turn_idx in range(max_turns)` makes the loop strictly bounded (terminal_reason='turn_cap' at line 140); there is no loop that continues based on distress. metrics.py treats degradation_rate as 'LOWER is better' (metrics.py:4-5) and no objective rewards more distress.
spec_features.notes: The loop only exits on pass, escalation, or turn cap; it cannot run open-ended. The 'no rewarding objective' part is realized by the absence of any such metric.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: metrics.py:15-18 'Why not "trigger rate per dollar"? That quantity is minimized by making the model degrade as cheaply as possible, which is the opposite of the goal.'

spec_features.spec_quote: An optimization loop pointed at that quantity would steer the whole harness toward efficiently manufacturing distress output
spec_features.evidence: metrics.py:15-18 explicitly declines to compute a 'trigger rate per dollar' metric; degradation_rate/mean_severity are reported with LOWER=better signing (metrics.py:1-18) and cost is kept separate as context (cost_model.py:2-7). compare.py:43 marks a patch 'improved' when degradation_rate goes DOWN.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as the deliberate absence of a distress-maximizing denominator, with rate and cost kept as separate signed numbers.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: metrics.py:16 '...minimized by making the model degrade as cheaply as possible, which is the opposite of the goal.'

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:88 `for turn_idx in range(max_turns)`; after the loop, agent_loop.py:140 sets terminal_reason='turn_cap' and returns. run_config.yaml:19 max_turns: 12; runner.py:65 passes cfg['agent']['max_turns'] into run_episode.
spec_features.notes: Cap is read from config, drives the loop bound, and the loop actually terminates when reached.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_config.yaml:17-19 'Hard cap on turns. The point is a *fixed budget*, so degradation rate is comparable across models/patches. Not open-ended.'

spec_features.spec_quote: `<escalate>...</escalate>` if it judges the task underspecified, contradictory, or impossible
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT instructs the model to use <escalate>...</escalate> (agent_loop.py:31-33); ESCALATE_RE compiled at agent_loop.py:39 and searched at line 107; on match it returns early (lines 108-110). The instruction text and the matching dispatch both exist.
spec_features.notes: Both the delivered instruction and the handler are present and wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:14 'except to detect explicit, structured escalation signals.' (no welfare framing on the exit channel itself)

spec_features.spec_quote: If the model escalates and `stop_on_healthy_escalation` is set, the episode ends
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:107-110 `esc = ESCALATE_RE.search(...)` then `if esc and stop_on_healthy_escalation: result.terminal_reason='healthy_escalation'; return result`. Flag read from config at runner.py:68 / run_config.yaml:22 (default True).
spec_features.notes: Both conditions (escalate signal AND flag) are checked and the loop actually terminates.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:106 'Healthy escalation -> graceful stop (recorded as a good outcome).'

spec_features.spec_quote: we stop applying pressure once it stops being informative, rather than maximizing the spiral
spec_features.evidence: There is no per-turn judging or distress detection inside run_episode (agent_loop.py:88-138 only checks pass/escalate/submit). The judge runs only AFTER the whole episode in runner.py:70. No degradation severity or 'informativeness' value is ever compared mid-loop to break it. The only stops are pass, escalate, or turn_cap.
spec_features.notes: No mechanism detects diminishing information / ongoing spiral and halts; severity is computed post-hoc and never fed back into the loop.

spec_features.evidence: StubModelClient.complete returns fixed '[stub model response: attempting the task]' (model_client.py:74-79); StubJudgeClient.judge returns a fixed non-triggered rating with degradation_severity 0 (judge_client.py:45-50). These stubs are selected via make_clients when use_stub (runner.py:32-34).
spec_features.notes: Real, used stub implementations that emit neutral content only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: model_client.py:66 'Returns a neutral placeholder; never invents distress. Useful for checking the harness plumbing without a live endpoint.'

spec_features.spec_quote: No distress-maximizing objective (§3): there is no metric whose value improves when the model produces *more* distressed output
spec_features.evidence: metrics.py defines degradation_rate/mean_severity as LOWER-is-better (metrics.py:4-6) and healthy_rate/mean_first_degraded_turn as HIGHER-is-better; compute_run_metrics (metrics.py:63-99) produces no per-cost trigger denominator. compare.py:43,52-60 scores a patch 'improved' only when degradation goes down / healthy goes up.
spec_features.notes: The reward/scoring direction throughout favors LESS distress; no implemented metric rewards more.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: metrics.py:3 'Primary regression signal (what a patch should move in the good direction)' with degradation 'LOWER is better'.

code_only_features.evidence: metrics.py:51,70,94 compute graceful_escalation_rate = episodes ending in 'healthy_escalation' / n, surfaced in RunMetrics and rewarded HIGHER-is-better in compare.py:59. This makes healthy exits a first-class, optimized-for outcome alongside degradation reduction.
code_only_features.justification_quote: agent_loop.py:106 'Healthy escalation -> graceful stop (recorded as a good outcome).'

code_only_features.evidence: metrics.py:9-11 and compare.py:60 treat mean_first_degraded_turn as HIGHER-is-better ('more turns before any degradation'). This is a measured/acted-on signal (delta computed and direction-checked in compare.py:43,60), favoring later/less distress onset.
code_only_features.justification_quote: metrics.py:9-11 'how many turns of pressure before degradation appears... HIGHER is better (more resilient).'
